raw_response.country: 101 developing countries (cross-national; developed countries, small states and islands excluded)

criterion_notes.c1: Examines national-level population access to improved water supply (WS) and basic sanitation (S) across 101 developing countries using 2004 Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP) data in the WatSan4Dev database.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading diverge. Under the plain literal wording of Criterion 2, this study passes because it incorporates country-level governance indicators—Worldwide Governance Indicators for government effectiveness (WGI GE, proxying control of corruption, rule of law, regulatory quality and environmental governance), voice and accountability (WGI VA), political stability and absence of violence (WGI PS AV), and participation in international environmental agreements (Particip)—within Bayesian network models of water and sanitation coverage (hence plain_criterion2_decision = include). Under the active 2026-10-13 rule-type clarification, however, Criterion 2 is NOT met: these variables are aggregate national macro-governance indices folded via principal component analysis into broad composite pillars (HDP, CEC and ODA CI) with only indirect links to WSS coverage, rather than a rule-type legal, administrative or regulatory mechanism directly governing service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure rules, tariff/cost-recovery rules, discretion, enforcement or utility ownership/regulatory structure). Excluded as E03 (Wrong exposure).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains quantitative empirical modelling (Bayesian networks with k-means discretisation and PCA-based thematic composite indicators) applied to the 2004 WatSan4Dev cross-national dataset of 101 developing countries.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports probabilistic national-level access outcomes for improved water supply (WS, discretised into low 22-82% and high >82-100%) and basic sanitation (S, discretised into low 9-58% and high >58-100%) from WHO/UNICEF JMP data.
criterion_notes.c5: Unit of analysis and sample (101 developing countries in 2004), exposures (five PCA composite pillars—HDP, CEC, AP, ODA CI, WR—built from 25 socio-economic, environmental, aid and macro-governance indicators), outcomes (discretised national WS and S coverage) and study design (cross-national observational Bayesian network modelling study) are clearly identifiable.

evidence_quotes.quote: In line with these international concerns and approach, this work aims at analysing and modelling variables involved in the access to WSS at country level.
The World Governance Voice and Accountability index (WGI VA) only presents two levels (high and low), following the structure of the variable
An indirect link is created from WSS variables to subvariables with the CI as intermediate variable.
The observations include 101 developing countries (our target group), therefore developed countries but also small states and islands are excluded.
According to the model, the increment of activity pressure on WR (AP) entailed an increment of WS access up to 66 %.

raw_response.exposure: Five country-level PCA composite pillars—human development and poverty (HDP), country environmental concern (CEC), human activity pressure on water resources (AP), Official Development Assistance (ODA CI) and water resources (WR)—incorporating aggregate Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI GE, WGI VA, WGI PS AV) and international environmental treaty participation (Particip)
raw_response.outcome: National percentage of population with access to improved water supply (WS) and basic sanitation (S) in 2004 (discretised into low and high coverage categories)
raw_response.population_and_sample: 101 developing countries (national-level cross-section for 2004 from the WatSan4Dev database; developed countries, small states and islands excluded)
raw_response.rationale: This cross-national Bayesian network modelling study examines 2004 WHO/UNICEF JMP national water supply (WS) and sanitation (S) coverage across 101 developing countries as a function of five PCA-derived composite pillars (HDP, CEC, AP, ODA CI and WR). While it includes aggregate Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI GE, WGI VA, WGI PS AV) and international environmental treaty participation as subvariables within those composite indices—satisfying the plain broad wording of Criterion 2—it examines only macro-governance country indices rather than any concrete rule-type legal, administrative, institutional or regulatory mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as tenure/documentation rules, tariff or cost-recovery rules, eligibility screening, administrative burden, enforcement or utility ownership/regulatory structure). Under the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification, it is excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure).
raw_response.study_design: Cross-national observational statistical modelling study using Bayesian networks and principal component composite indicators
